query_elements.name: query_elements
query_elements.description: Query elements of a category after applying optional filters and return selected parameter fields.

aggregate_elements.name: aggregate_elements
aggregate_elements.description: Aggregate elements of a category (count, sum, avg, min, max) after applying optional filters, optionally grouped by a parameter.

list_audit_rules.name: list_audit_rules
list_audit_rules.description: List all available BIM audit rules.

run_audit.name: run_audit
run_audit.description: Run a specific BIM audit rule and return the elements that violate it.

rule_name.description: The exact name of the audit rule to run.

run_generated_snippet.name: run_generated_snippet
run_generated_snippet.description: Run a short READ-ONLY Python 2.7 snippet against the open Revit model, for relationships, distances, combining categories, comparisons or multi-step logic that query_elements, aggregate_elements or run_audit cannot do. Use only revit_ro (lengths in metres, areas in m2): get_elements(category) returns a list of {id, name, category} (name is Revit's element name, e.g. the type name for walls and doors, not the Mark) for Doors, Windows, Walls, Rooms, Levels or Columns ('Columns' is Revit's Structural Columns category); get_param(element_id, name) returns the value (numbers in m, m2, m3; 'Type Name' gives the type name; None if missing); get_geometry_bbox(element_id) returns {min: [x, y, z], max: [x, y, z], center: [x, y, z]} or None; get_line(element_id) returns {start: [x, y, z], end: [x, y, z], length_m} for walls and other line-based elements, {point: [x, y, z]} for point-based elements such as doors and columns, or None; get_relationship(door_id, 'rooms_bounding_door') returns {from_room_id, to_room_id}; get_level_of_element(element_id) returns the level name; get_host_id(element_id) returns the host id or None. list_levels() returns [{id, name, elevation_m}]; list_wall_types() returns wall type names; list_family_types(category) returns the 'Family: Type' names LOADED in the project (Doors, Windows, Columns, Furniture and the other family categories), not only the ones already placed. Same Python subset as action snippets (no import, while, try, lambda, def, **, isinstance, % formatting; 5 s timeout). Assign the answer to result.

code.description: Short Python code using only revit_ro. The code must assign the final answer to a variable named result.

propose_set_parameter.name: propose_set_parameter
propose_set_parameter.description: Propose setting ONE parameter to ONE value on specific elements. This does NOT change the model: it creates a proposal the user must confirm with a button. element_ids must be the _id values returned by earlier query_elements or run_audit results. If the user has not said which value to use, ask.

audit_name.description: Optional. The audit rule this fix is for, e.g. missing_fire_rating.

query_past_changes.name: query_past_changes
query_past_changes.description: Previously APPLIED changes made by this agent, newest first. Use for 'what did we do last time?' questions. All parameters are optional.

select_elements.name: select_elements
select_elements.description: Select elements of a category in the Revit user interface, after applying optional filters (same filters as query_elements). This only changes which elements are selected on screen; it does not modify the model and needs no confirmation. Returns how many elements were selected and their IDs.

propose_action.name: propose_action
propose_action.description: Create ONE proposed model change (at most one per user message) from a short Python 2.7 snippet that uses only the revit_rw methods: get_param, set_param, get_location, get_line, list_levels, list_wall_types, list_types, list_family_types, create_wall, change_type, move_element, copy_element, delete_elements, place_door, place_window, rotate_element, mirror_element, place_instance, create_level, create_grid, create_floor_in_room, create_floor, create_ceiling_in_room. Follow the limits, the NOT AVAILABLE list and the SNIPPET PYTHON rules in the system prompt; never split a request to get past a limit. The snippet first runs as a dry run that is rolled back, and the exact changes are shown to the user on a card; nothing is applied unless the user clicks Confirm. A snippet that only sets result makes no change and returns data (use it only to read data, never to return a message). Assign a short summary to result.

description.description: One short sentence describing the change for the user.

code.description: The Python 2.7 snippet, using only the revit_rw methods listed above.

view_action.name: view_action
view_action.description: Change only the DISPLAY of the active Revit view, never the model: action 'isolate' or 'hide' (temporary), 'zoom' (zoom the view to the elements) or 'reset' (turn off temporary hide/isolate). Target elements by category with optional filters (same as query_elements) or by element_ids. Runs immediately; no confirmation is needed.
